title: Rav Ika son of Rav Idi

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Bava Kamma 12a, but Hyman calls this a scribal error and says the reading should be “son of Rav Ami,” as explained in his entry.[^1]

notes.text: The actual Davidson Bava Kamma 12a paragraph explicitly writes Rav Ika son of Rav Ami. Hyman’s heading Idi and his emphatic scribal-error/should-read claim remain distinct from that digital Ami reading; no father or identity merge or correction-history proof is admitted.
